title: Unit 2 test: Differentiation: Definition and Fundamental Properties
author: bc-tests-foundation
directions: This original practice test reports raw points only. Work without a calculator in Section I Part A and Section II Part B. A graphing calculator is allowed in the other parts. Angles are in radians. Give exact answers without a calculator and numerical answers to three decimal places when needed. Show mathematical reasoning on every free-response part.

figures.alt: Graph of f made of line segments joining filled points (−2, 3), (1, 0), and (3, 4).

parts.title: No calculator
parts.directions: Choose one answer for each question. No calculator is allowed.

items.prompt: Which derivative is represented by lim as h→0 of (√(9 + h) − 3)/h?
items.rationale: The numerator is f(9 + h) − f(9), so the quotient defines f′(9) for f(x) = √x.

distractorNotes.A: The numerator contains square-root values, not square values.
distractorNotes.C: Confuses the function value 3 with the input 9.
distractorNotes.D: Uses the limiting increment as the base input.

items.prompt: The graph of f consists of two line segments. What is f′(0)?
items.rationale: The segment containing x = 0 has slope (0 − 3)/(1 − (−2)) = −1.

distractorNotes.A: Uses the slope of the right-hand segment.
distractorNotes.B: The corner is at x = 1, not at x = 0.
distractorNotes.C: The value of the derivative is the segment slope, not the x-coordinate.

distractorNotes.B: Omits the exponent factor 2 when differentiating x^(−2), giving −3 + 2.
distractorNotes.C: Loses the negative sign in the reciprocal-power derivative.

items.prompt: The differentiable functions f and g satisfy f(2) = 3, f′(2) = −1, g(2) = 4, and g′(2) = 5. If P = fg, what is P′(2)?

distractorNotes.B: Multiplies the derivatives instead of using the product rule.
Divides the numerator derivative by the denominator derivative.
distractorNotes.D: Reverses the two numerator terms in the quotient rule.

items.prompt: If y = sec x, what is dy/dx at x = π/3?
items.rationale: The derivative is sec x tan x. At π/3 these factors are 2 and √3.

distractorNotes.A: Uses sec x without the tan x factor.
distractorNotes.C: Uses tan x without the sec x factor.
distractorNotes.D: Adds a negative sign to the derivative of sec x.

items.prompt: For x > 0, let f(x) = x ln x − x. What is f′(e)?
items.rationale: The product rule gives f′(x) = ln x + 1 − 1 = ln x, so f′(e) = 1.

distractorNotes.A: Uses the input e itself rather than evaluating the derivative.
distractorNotes.B: Cancels derivatives as if the derivative of x ln x were only 1.
distractorNotes.C: Differentiates x ln x correctly but forgets the derivative of −x.

items.prompt: Let f(x) = |x − 2| + 3. Which statement describes f at x = 2?
choices: It is continuous but not differentiable.
It is both continuous and differentiable.
It is neither continuous nor differentiable.
It is differentiable but not continuous.
items.rationale: The one-sided values both approach 3 = f(2), but the one-sided slopes differ.

distractorNotes.B: The left and right slopes are −1 and 1, not equal.
distractorNotes.C: The two sides meet at the defined value 3, so continuity holds.
distractorNotes.D: Differentiability implies continuity, and the corner prevents differentiability.

parts.title: Graphing calculator
parts.directions: Choose one answer for each question. A graphing calculator is needed for some numerical work.

items.prompt: For f(x) = x^2 sin x, which value best approximates f′(1.4)?
items.rationale: The product rule gives f′(x) = 2x sin x + x^2 cos x; evaluating at 1.4 gives 3.092.

distractorNotes.A: Evaluates f(1.4) instead of its derivative.
distractorNotes.B: Keeps only the term 2x sin x.
distractorNotes.D: Keeps only the term x^2 cos x.

items.prompt: What is the slope of the tangent to y = e^x − 2x at x = 0.7, to three decimal places?
items.rationale: The derivative is e^x − 2, so the slope is e^0.7 − 2 ≈ 0.014.

distractorNotes.B: Treats the derivative of e^x as the constant 1.
distractorNotes.C: Uses the function value e^0.7 − 1.4 rather than the derivative.

items.prompt:
A smooth function has the values below. Using the secant through the two closest inputs on opposite sides of 3, estimate f′(3).
x | 2.90 | 2.97 | 3.03 | 3.10
f(x) | 5.40 | 5.814 | 6.186 | 6.66

distractorNotes.A: Uses the farther pair rather than the specified closest pair.
distractorNotes.C: Divides by 0.03 even though the two inputs are 0.06 apart.
distractorNotes.D: Finds the output change but does not divide by the input change.

items.prompt: For f(x) = x^3 − 2.3x^2 + sin x, which x in [1, 2] gives a horizontal tangent, to three decimal places?
items.rationale: A horizontal tangent requires 3x^2 − 4.6x + cos x = 0. The graphing-calculator solution on [1, 2] is 1.523.

distractorNotes.A: Uses the interval endpoint without satisfying the zero-slope condition.
distractorNotes.B: Ignores the cosine term in the derivative.
distractorNotes.C: Does not solve the derivative equation; the derivative there is positive.

parts.title: Graphing calculator
parts.directions: Show the equations used for numerical results and include units where appropriate.

items.prompt: A sensor model gives electrical power P(t) = t ln t watts for 1 ≤ t ≤ 5, with t measured in seconds.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find P′(2.4). Explain its meaning with units.

rubric.criterion: Obtains P′(t) = ln t + 1 using the product rule.
Interprets the instantaneous rate at 2.4 seconds with W/s.

parts.answer: 1.875 W/s; this is the instantaneous rate of increase of power at 2.4 seconds.
steps: Use the product rule: P′(t) = ln t + 1.
Power is measured in watts, so its time derivative is measured in watts per second.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write an equation of the tangent line to the graph of P at t = 2.4.

rubric.criterion: Uses the derivative as the slope.
Writes a line passing through that point with the correct slope.

steps: Use point-slope form; an exact logarithmic form is also accepted.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of P from t = 1 to t = 5. Is it greater than or less than P′(2.4)? Support your comparison.

rubric.criterion: Sets up the secant quotient correctly.
Makes the correct comparison with supporting values.

steps: Compare the average and instantaneous rates numerically.

parts.title: No calculator
parts.directions: Show your reasoning and give exact answers. No calculator is allowed.

items.prompt: Let f(x) = ax + b for x < 1 and f(x) = x^2 + 2x for x ≥ 1, where a and b are constants.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the condition on a and b that makes f continuous at 1. Justify it.

rubric.criterion: Finds the right-hand limit and point value.
Equates these values to obtain a + b = 3.

steps: The left-hand limit is a + b.
The right-hand limit and the defined value f(1) both equal 3.
Set the left-hand limit equal to that value.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine a and b so that f is differentiable at 1. Use a difference quotient to find the derivative from the right.

rubric.criterion: Sets up and simplifies the right-hand difference quotient.
Matches the limiting right slope with a = 4.

steps: The right derivative is 4; the left derivative must be a = 4.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Use the values from part (b). Let g(x) = f(x) sin x. Find g′(0), showing the derivative rule used.

rubric.criterion: Selects the correct branch and its value and slope at zero.
Applies the product and sine derivative rules.

steps: Near zero, f(x) = 4x − 1, so f(0) = −1 and f′(0) = 4.
